```text
hi @ojcchar, a few questions on #131 before we finish the spec. we put what we'd do next to each one, just tell us if that's fine or what you want instead. 1 and 2 block us.

1. if someone logs in with oidc and their email already has a cal.diy account, what should happen? we think auto link only if the admin says the provider owns that email domain, otherwise reject and make them link it from settings. never auto link an admin account.
2. who can make a new account through oidc? we think a per provider "allow new accounts" switch (off by default) plus an optional list of allowed domains. should the existing "disable signup" setting block oidc signup too?
3. if the provider doesn't send email_verified, we reject the login. ok?
4. do you want a switch to turn off password login? if so admins would always keep password login so nobody gets locked out. we'd do this in sprint 4.
5. if an admin removes a provider people use, we show how many users it affects, make them type the name to confirm, and those users can use forgot password to get back in. ok?
6. should the require 2fa setting apply to oidc users too, or does the provider's mfa count?
7. if someone's email changes at the provider, we update it in cal.diy if it's verified and not taken. ok?
8. if someone was invited but hasn't accepted yet, should an oidc login with that email take over the invite, or treat it like 1?
9. no mapping provider groups to cal.diy roles for now. ok?
10. users can unlink a provider unless it's their only way to log in. ok?
11. is up to 10 providers enough?
12. we're testing with keycloak locally. is that ok or do you want authentik or okta too?
13. after upgrading nothing changes until an admin adds a provider. ok?

thanks!

--
author:	ojcchar
association:	contributor
edited:	false
status:	none
--
These are good questions, and your proposals are mostly what we want.

1. Agreed: auto-link only when the email is verified and the admin marked the provider as owning that domain. Otherwise reject and let the user link it from settings. Never auto-link admin accounts.
2. Agreed on the per-provider switch (off by default) and the allowed domains. Yes, the global "disable signup" setting also blocks OIDC sign-up, and it wins over the provider switch. An admin who turned off sign-up expects no new accounts from anywhere. They can still let people in by inviting them (see 8).
3. Yes, reject the login if email_verified is missing or false.
4. Yes, in Sprint 4. Admins always keep password login.
5. Fine, but check one thing: users created through OIDC have no password, so make sure "forgot password" actually works for them, and test it. Also let admins disable a provider instead of deleting it.
6. We'd like users to rely on the provider's MFA when it can be checked. Add a per-provider setting, "accept this provider's MFA." When it's on and the ID token's amr claim shows a second factor, skip Cal.diy's 2FA. If amr is missing or shows only a password, require Cal.diy's 2FA. This can be in Sprint 4.
7. Fine, as long as accounts are matched by the provider's user ID (the sub claim), never by email. If the new email is already taken, keep the old one and tell the user.
8. A verified OIDC login with an invited email accepts the invite, even if "allow new accounts" is off for that provider.
9. Agreed, no group mapping for now.
10. Agreed.
11. Yes, 10 is enough.
12. Keycloak is fine. Document the setup so anyone on the team can run the tests.
13. Agreed.
```

```text
Sign in with any OIDC provider (Keycloak, Authentik, Okta) on self-hosted instances
### Is your proposal related to a problem?

Self-hosted Cal.diy only supports email and password, Google, and Microsoft login. Organizations that host Cal.diy usually have their own login system (an identity provider such as Keycloak, Authentik, or Okta). Their staff need a separate password for Cal.diy.

### Describe the solution you would like

Support login with any OpenID Connect (OIDC) provider, configured by an admin. The spec below is a starting point. The acceptance criteria are incomplete, and the open questions must be answered before implementation.

### User Story

As an admin of a self-hosted Cal.diy instance, I want users to log in with our organization's identity provider so that they don't need a separate password and access follows our existing accounts.

### User Scenario

An IT admin connects Cal.diy to the university's login system. A professor clicks "Continue with University SSO" on the login page, signs in on the university's page, and comes back to Cal.diy logged in.

### Acceptance Criteria (draft, incomplete)

- [ ] An admin can add, edit, and remove OIDC providers from the admin settings page, without changing environment variables or restarting the server.
- [ ] Users see a "Continue with <provider></provider>" button on the login page and can log in with it.
- [ ] If the provider doesn't return a verified email, the login is rejected and the user sees a clear message.
- [ ] More criteria needed, based on the open questions below.

Acceptance criteria should also cover invalid input, failures, conflicts, and permissions, not only the main path.

### Out of Scope

- Changes to SAML login
- Logging out of the identity provider (single logout)

### Open Questions

- A user logs in with OIDC and an account with the same email already exists. What happens? How do we prevent someone from taking over another person's account?
- Who may create an account through OIDC: anyone at the provider, or only some email domains?
- What does the user see if the provider is down or misconfigured?
- Can there be more than one provider? Can admins turn off password login?
- How are provider secrets stored, and who can see them?
- Can a user unlink their OIDC login? What if it is their only way to log in?
- Should groups from the provider give users Cal.diy roles (for example, admin)?
- How do we test this without a real company identity provider?
- What happens to existing data and installations after upgrading?

### Additional context

Areas this touches: provider configuration (admin), the login and sign-up flow, account creation and linking, user account settings, and test setup.

### Requirement/Document

- How OpenID Connect works: https://openid.net/developers/how-connect-works/
enhancement,effort:high,scope: large
Sprint 3
```

```text
  getDubId,

    // decorate the native JWT encode function
    // Impl. detail: We don't pass through as this function is called with encode/decode functions.
    encode: async ({ token, maxAge, secret }) => {
      log.debug("jwt:encode", safeStringify({ token, maxAge }));
      if (token?.sub && isNumber(token.sub)) {
        const user = await prisma.user.findFirst({
          where: { id: Number(token.sub) },
          select: { metadata: true },
        });
        // if no user is found, we still don't want to crash here.
        if (user) {
          const metadata = userMetadata.parse(user.metadata);
          if (metadata?.sessionTimeout) {
            maxAge = metadata.sessionTimeout * 60;
          }
        }
      }
      return encode({ secret, token, maxAge });
    },
  },
```

```text
import { IdentityProvider } from "@calcom/prisma/enums";

/**
 * Maps NextAuth provider names to IdentityProvider enum values.
 * Includes aliases (e.g., "saml-idp" -> SAML).
 */
export const NEXTAUTH_TO_IDENTITY_PROVIDER: Record<string, IdentityProvider> = {
  "azure-ad": IdentityProvider.AZUREAD,
  google: IdentityProvider.GOOGLE,
  saml: IdentityProvider.SAML,
  "saml-idp": IdentityProvider.SAML,
  cal: IdentityProvider.CAL,
};

/**
 * Get IdentityProvider enum from NextAuth provider name.
 * Returns null for unknown providers so callers can reject the login gracefully.
 */
export const getIdentityProvider = (nextAuthProvider: string): IdentityProvider | null => {
  return NEXTAUTH_TO_IDENTITY_PROVIDER[nextAuthProvider] ?? null;
};
```

```text
import type { NextApiRequest, NextApiResponse } from "next";
import NextAuth from "next-auth";

import { getOptions } from "@calcom/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options";
import { getTrackingFromCookies } from "@calcom/lib/tracking";

// pass req to NextAuth: https://github.com/nextauthjs/next-auth/discussions/469
const handler = (req: NextApiRequest, res: NextApiResponse) =>
  NextAuth(
    req,
    res,
    getOptions({
      getDubId: () => req.cookies.dub_id || req.cookies.dclid,
      getTrackingData: () => getTrackingFromCookies(req.cookies, req.query),
    })
  );
```

# Issue #131: Sign in with any OIDC provider on self-hosted instances

Your reading is right. An admin of a self-hosted cal.diy (say, W&M IT) connects it to the organization's existing login system (Keycloak, Okta, Authentik, a university SSO). Users then click "Continue with University SSO" instead of keeping a separate cal.diy password.

One thing to flag first: the instructor wants a demo that works end to end, from UI to server, by **Nov 19**. That's one week from today. I've marked which phases need to be in that demo.

---

## 1. How OpenID Connect (OIDC) works

OIDC is a thin identity layer on top of OAuth 2.0. OAuth answers "may this app access my stuff?" OIDC adds "who is this person?"

**The three parties:**
- **The user**, in a browser.
- **The relying party (RP)**, which is cal.diy here.
- **The OpenID Provider (OP)**, also called the IdP. This is Keycloak, Okta, or the university SSO.

**One-time setup (what the admin does):**
1. The IdP admin registers cal.diy as a "client". They get a **client ID** and a **client secret**, and they whitelist cal.diy's **redirect URI** (for example `https://cal.example.edu/api/auth/callback/oidc-university`).
2. The cal.diy admin enters the **issuer URL**, client ID and secret. cal.diy then fetches `<issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration`, the **discovery document**. It lists every endpoint cal.diy needs (authorize, token, userinfo, signing keys), so the admin doesn't have to type any of them.

**Each login (the "Authorization Code flow"):**
```
Browser ──click "Continue with SSO"──▶ cal.diy
cal.diy ──302 redirect──▶ IdP /authorize?client_id=…&redirect_uri=…&scope=openid email profile
                           &state=<random>&nonce=<random>&code_challenge=<PKCE>
User logs in at the IdP (password, MFA, whatever the IdP requires; cal.diy never sees this)
IdP ──302 redirect──▶ cal.diy /callback?code=<one-time code>&state=…
cal.diy ──server-to-server POST──▶ IdP /token (code + client secret + PKCE verifier)
IdP ──▶ { access_token, id_token }
cal.diy verifies the id_token's signature (IdP's public keys), issuer, audience, expiry, nonce
```

`state`, `nonce` and PKCE are anti-forgery and anti-replay checks.

**The ID token** is a signed JWT of "claims". These are the ones that matter for this issue:

| Claim | Meaning | Why the client cares |
|---|---|---|
| `iss` | Which IdP issued it | Identifies the provider |
| `sub` | The IdP's permanent, unique user ID | **The client wants accounts matched by `sub`, never by email** (answer 7) |
| `email` / `email_verified` | The user's email, and whether the IdP checked it | Reject if `email_verified` is missing or false (answer 3) |
| `amr` | Authentication methods used (`pwd`, `otp`, `mfa`, `hwk`, …) | Lets cal.diy skip its own 2FA when the IdP already did MFA (answer 6) |
| `name`, `picture` | Profile info | Fills in the new user's profile |

The key point is that the IdP never gives cal.diy the user's password. cal.diy gets a signed statement: "this is user `sub` at issuer `iss`, their verified email is X, and they authenticated with Y." Because OIDC is a standard, one generic implementation works with any compliant IdP. That's why the issue says "any OIDC provider".

---

## 2. What the client is asking for

**Core feature (issue body):** Admins can add, edit, and remove OIDC providers from the admin settings UI. This must not require env vars or a server restart. Users see a "Continue with \<provider\>" button on the login page. A login without a verified email is rejected with a clear message. SAML changes and single logout are out of scope.

**Decisions from the comment thread:**

| # | Topic | Client's answer |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Existing account with the same email | Auto-link **only** if `email_verified` is true **and** the admin marked the provider as owning that email domain. Otherwise reject, and the user links it from settings. **Never auto-link admin accounts.** |
| 2 | Who can create accounts | Each provider has an "allow new accounts" switch (**off by default**) plus an optional allowed-domains list. The global **"disable signup" setting wins** over everything. |
| 3 | `email_verified` missing or false | Reject. |
| 4 | Turn off password login | Yes, in **Sprint 4**. Admins always keep password login. |
| 5 | Removing a provider | Show how many users it affects and require typing the name to confirm. Also add **disable as an alternative to delete**. Verify that **forgot password actually works for OIDC-created users** (they have no password), and test it. |
| 6 | 2FA | A per-provider setting, "accept this provider's MFA". When it's on and `amr` shows a second factor, skip cal.diy 2FA. Otherwise require it. **Sprint 4.** |
| 7 | Email changes at the IdP | Match by `sub`, never by email. Update the email if it's verified and not taken. If it's taken, keep the old one and tell the user. |
| 8 | Pending invites | A verified OIDC login with an invited email **accepts the invite**, even if "allow new accounts" is off. Answer 2 also implies this works when signup is disabled. |
| 9 | Group-to-role mapping | No. |
| 10 | Unlinking | Allowed, unless it's the user's only way to log in. |
| 11 | Provider limit | 10. |
| 12 | Test IdP | Keycloak, with the setup **documented** so anyone on the team can run it. |
| 13 | Upgrade behavior | Nothing changes until an admin adds a provider. |

**Process requirements:** finish the spec (including failure, permission, and old-data cases), split the work into sub-issues with owners, specs, and spec reviews, post the breakdown on the issue, and demo end to end by Nov 19.

**Cases the issue lists that the thread hasn't answered yet.** The instructor said "don't guess; ask," so these probably need a follow-up comment:
- What the user sees when the IdP is down or misconfigured (discovery fetch fails, timeout, bad client secret, issuer mismatch).
- Who can see the client secret. I'd suggest it's write-only: never returned to the UI once saved.
- Whether an admin can edit a provider's ID/slug. The redirect URI registered at the IdP contains it, so changing it breaks login. I'd suggest making it immutable.
- What happens if the issuer URL changes. `sub` is only unique per issuer, so existing links could silently point at the wrong people.
- Whether a locked cal.diy account (the `locked` flag) blocks OIDC login. Presumably yes.

---

## 3. Systems in the code this touches

| System | Where | What I found |
|---|---|---|
| **NextAuth config** | `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` (1,255 lines) | Providers are a **static array built at module load from env vars** (`:307-370`: Credentials, Google, AzureAD, Email). This is the main architectural obstacle to "no restart". The good news is that `apps/web/pages/api/auth/[...nextauth].ts` already calls `getOptions()` **per request**, so providers *can* become per-request. |
| **Sign-in policy** | Same file: `signIn` callback (`:808-1180`) | It handles verification, linking and user creation for Google/Azure/SAML. Its self-hosted path **auto-merges on any verified email** (`:1011`), which is looser than client rule #1. OIDC needs its own, stricter path that never falls into that logic. |
| **Provider-name mapping** | `packages/features/auth/lib/identityProviders.ts` | It maps NextAuth IDs to the `IdentityProvider` enum and returns `null` for unknown IDs, so logins from an `oidc-*` provider would currently be rejected. |
| **Schema** | `packages/prisma/schema.prisma` | `IdentityProvider` enum (`:367`: CAL, GOOGLE, SAML, AZUREAD). `User.identityProvider`/`identityProviderId` hold only **one** provider per user. `Account` (`:1241`) already supports **many** links per user, keyed `@@unique([provider, providerAccountId])`, which is the natural home for (provider, `sub`). There's no table for provider config yet. |
| **Secret storage** | `packages/lib/crypto.ts` (`symmetricEncrypt`) | The existing pattern encrypts with `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, as `Deployment.signatureTokenEncrypted` already does. |
| **Signup gate** | `apps/web/app/api/auth/signup/route.ts:29-31` | It checks the `NEXT_PUBLIC_DISABLE_SIGNUP` env var **and** the `disable-signup` feature flag. OIDC account creation must apply the same check. |
| **2FA** | `isTwoFactorRequiredSiteWide.ts`, `requiresTwoFactorSetup.ts`, jwt callback (`:524`) | This is where "accept provider MFA" would plug in (Sprint 4). |
| **Admin UI** | `apps/web/app/(use-page-wrapper)/settings/(admin-layout)/admin/*` (`security`, `users`, `flags`, …) | A new admin "SSO/OIDC" page goes here. |
| **Admin API** | `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/admin/_router.ts` | New CRUD procedures go here. Business logic goes in a `packages/features` service and repository, per the repo's rules. |
| **Login page** | `apps/web/modules/auth/login-view.tsx` (Google button at `:207`, Azure at `:224`) | Add dynamic provider buttons here. |
| **Error page** | `/auth/error?error=…` | Add new error codes and messages. |
| **User settings** | `apps/web/modules/settings/security/password-view.tsx` (`:152` already handles non-CAL users with no password), `my-account/profile-view.tsx` | Add a linked-providers section with link and unlink. |
| **Forgot password** | `apps/web/app/api/auth/forgot-password/route.ts`, `passwordResetRequest.ts` | It looks users up by email only. It probably works for passwordless users, but the client explicitly wants this verified and tested. |
| **Invites** | `User.invitedTo` + team memberships with `accepted: false` | Needed for rule 8. |
| **i18n** | `packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json` | All new strings go here. |

---

## 4. High-level phases

File counts are code plus tests. Effort is relative: **S** ≈ under a day, **M** ≈ 1–3 days, **L** ≈ 3–5 days for one person.

### Phase 0: Spec, sub-issues, Keycloak test setup ★ Sprint 3
Finish the spec, post the breakdown, and ask the follow-up questions above. Add a `docker-compose` Keycloak service with a pre-built realm export (a test client and users with verified and unverified emails), plus a setup doc. Do this first so everyone can test against a real IdP from day one.
**~3–4 files** (compose, realm JSON, doc) · **S–M**

### Phase 1: Data layer ★ Sprint 3
- Add a **provider-config table**. One row per provider: immutable slug, display name, issuer URL, client ID, **encrypted** client secret, scopes, enabled/disabled, allow-new-accounts, allowed signup domains, "owned" domains for auto-link, accept-provider-MFA, timestamps.
- Add **`OIDC` to the `IdentityProvider` enum**.
- Store per-user links in the existing **`Account` table** as (`oidc-<slug>`, `sub`). That gives you multiple providers per user, matching by `sub`, and unlinking.
- Add a migration (additive only, so rule 13 holds automatically).
- Add a repository and DTOs.

Schema changes are "ask first" under the repo rules, so get a design review on this one.
**~5–7 files** · **M**

### Phase 2: Provider admin backend ★ Sprint 3 (CRUD) / Sprint 4 (polish)
- A service that validates input. It fetches the discovery document on save, so a bad issuer fails right away, and it checks the 10-provider cap and unique slugs.
- It encrypts the secret on write and **never returns it**.
- It supports disable versus delete, and counts the users affected by a delete.
- Admin-only tRPC procedures wrap the service.
- A **public** read endpoint returns only the enabled providers' slug and display name, for the login page.

**~7–10 files** · **M**

### Phase 3: Dynamic provider registration ★ Sprint 3 (hardest technical piece)
Change `getOptions()` so that on each request it appends a generic NextAuth OAuth provider for every **enabled** DB provider. Each uses `wellKnown` discovery, `idToken: true`, and `state`/`nonce`/PKCE checks, so NextAuth handles the protocol. Also teach `identityProviders.ts` that `oidc-*` maps to `OIDC`, and probably add a short cache so every request doesn't hit the DB.

This affects every login, including password login, so it carries regression risk.
**~3–5 files** · **M–L**

### Phase 4: OIDC sign-in policy ★ Sprint 3 (main path) / Sprint 4 (the rest)
This is the core logic and most of the security surface. Put it in a dedicated `OidcSignInService` that the `signIn` callback hands off to early, so OIDC never touches the existing auto-merge code. The decision tree:

1. Reject if `email_verified` is not true.
2. Find an existing link by (provider, `sub`). If one exists, log in that user. If the email changed, sync it when it's free; otherwise keep the old one and show a notice.
3. If there's no link but the email matches an existing user:
   - Accept a pending **invite** (rule 8).
   - Otherwise auto-link only if the provider "owns" the domain **and** the user isn't an admin.
   - Otherwise reject with "link it from settings".
4. If the email is new: block if global disable-signup is on, the provider's "allow new accounts" is off, or the domain isn't allowed. Otherwise create the user with no password and link them.
5. Handle the failure cases: locked account, provider disabled mid-flow, IdP errors. Each maps to a specific `/auth/error` code and message.

The Sprint 3 demo needs only rules 1, 2, and the new-account branch of 4. Linking and invites can follow.
**~5–8 files** (service, callback wiring, error codes, heavy unit tests) · **L**

### Phase 5: Login page and error UX ★ Sprint 3
Render a "Continue with \<name\>" button for each enabled provider, and add error-page messages for each new code. All strings go in i18n.
**~4–5 files** · **S**

### Phase 6: Admin settings UI ★ Sprint 3 (basic add/list) / Sprint 4 (full)
A new admin page with a provider list, an add/edit form (secret is write-only; the page shows the redirect URI to paste into the IdP), a disable toggle, and delete with the affected-user count and type-the-name confirmation.
**~4–6 files** · **M**

### Phase 7: User account settings (Sprint 4)
A "Connected logins" section that lists linked providers, a **link** button (OIDC sign-in while already logged in, which attaches the `sub` to the current user), and an **unlink** button guarded by "not your only login method" (rule 10). Linking while logged in has its own edge cases, such as a `sub` that's already linked to someone else.
**~5–7 files** · **M**

### Phase 8: Sprint 4 policy features
- An admin "disable password login" switch, with admins exempt.
- "Accept provider MFA" through the `amr` claim in the 2FA path.
- Verify and test the forgot-password flow for passwordless OIDC users.

**~6–9 files** · **M–L**

### Phase 9: Tests and docs (ongoing, ★ partly Sprint 3)
Unit tests ship with each phase. Add one or two Playwright e2e tests against the Keycloak container (admin adds a provider, then a user logs in), plus admin and self-host docs.
**~5–8 files** · **M**

## 5. Overall estimate

| | Files | Effort |
|---|---|---|
| Sprint 3 slice (0, 1, 2-core, 3, 4-main, 5, 6-basic, some 9) | ~30–40 | Roughly 3–4 people for a week. Tight. |
| Sprint 4 remainder (2-polish, 4-rest, 6-full, 7, 8, rest of 9) | ~20–30 | Similar |
| **Total** | **~50–65 files, ~3,000–4,500 lines with tests** | **Large.** The issue's `effort:high` / `scope: large` labels fit. |

**Two things to plan around:**
- **PR size.** The repo caps PRs at 500 lines and 10 files, so this is roughly 8–12 PRs. The phases above map well onto sub-issues and PRs. Phases 3 and 4 are on the critical path: nothing can be demoed until login actually works.
- **Risk.** Phases 3 and 4 change the login path for every user, and Phase 4 is where account-takeover bugs would live. Those two deserve your strongest reviewers and the most tests. Phase 0 (Keycloak) should land first so everyone can test in parallel.

```text
# #131 sub-issue breakdown (draft)

Draft for the team. After the team fills the Owner column, paste the "Comment for #131" section as a comment on #131. Then create one sub-issue per row; each owner writes the full spec in their sub-issue before code, and a teammate posts a spec review.

Full spec: `specs/oidc-sign-in/design.md` (criteria numbers below refer to it). Decisions: `decisions.md`.

## Rules for every sub-issue

- One GitHub assignee, who writes or refines the sub-issue spec before code. The spec states its scope (small or medium) and one or two sentences on why.
- Link each sub-issue to #131 and attach it to the Sprint 3 milestone. Sub-issues count toward each member's two-medium-issue minimum.
- A spec-review comment from another teammate before implementation. It must say what was checked: each acceptance criterion clear and testable, which cases were considered, whether the scope fits. "Looks good" alone does not count.
- One PR under 500 changed lines and under 10 code files. The description has `Closes #<sub-issue>`, the Tech Debt section and the Test Evidence table (one row per criterion; expected values come from the criterion, never from the code's output).
- Merge only after a teammate approves the latest commit. After that approval the author may merge. Request the review on GitHub and tell the reviewer on Zulip; reviewers answer within 24 hours.
- Sprint 3 replaces UML diagrams with mutation testing (StrykerJS with the Vitest runner) on one of each member's issues. Rows 1, 3 and 5 have the most unit-testable logic for this.
- Zach Bowden cannot run the Next.js dev server. Rows 1, 3 and 5 can be verified with unit tests alone; rows 4, 6 and 8 need a browser.

## Comment for #131

---

**Breakdown of #131 into sub-issues**

Full draft spec (acceptance criteria, edge cases, proposed answers, decisions with alternatives): `specs/oidc-sign-in/` on branch `docs/oidc-spec`. Our questions for you are in the next comment.

| # | Sub-issue | Area in #131 | Size | Depends on | Sprint | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | OIDC provider data model and repository | Provider configuration | M | none | 3 | |
| 2 | Local Keycloak test provider and realm | Test setup | S | none | 3 | |
| 3 | Admin provider service and tRPC procedures | Provider configuration | M | 1 | 3 | |
| 4 | Admin "Identity providers" settings page | Provider configuration | M | 3 | 3 | |
| 5 | Load providers per request and create new OIDC users | Login and sign-up | M | 1 | 3 | |
| 6 | Login page buttons and sign-in error messages | Login and sign-up | S | 5 | 3 | |
| 7 | Link OIDC to existing accounts (rule from customer) | Account creation and linking | M | 5, customer Q1 | 4 | |
| 8 | Connected logins in Settings → Security (link, unlink) | User account settings | M | 7 | 4 | |
| 9 | Provider removal, password-login switch, end-to-end tests | Provider configuration, test setup | M | 4, 7 | 4 | |

**Sprint 3 demo (by Nov 19):** an admin adds a Keycloak provider in admin settings (secret stored encrypted), the login page shows "Continue with <name>", a user with a verified email signs in and gets a new account, and a user with an unverified email sees a clear error. A login whose email matches an existing account is rejected for now, which is safe under every answer to our linking question. Merge order: 1 first; then 3 and 5 in parallel; then 4 (after 3) and 6 (after 5). Row 2 can merge at any time.

---

## Sub-issue seeds

Each seed is the starting spec. The owner expands it into a full issue (story, scenario, numbered criteria, out of scope, design decisions with two alternatives) like #130.

### 1. OIDC provider data model and repository (M, Sprint 3)

Add `OIDC` to `enum IdentityProvider` and a new `OidcProvider` model (fields in design.md, Database Changes) with a migration. Add `PrismaOidcProviderRepository` (`findEnabled`, `findById`, `list`, `create`, `update`, `delete`, `countLinkedUsers`) using `select`, never `include`, and wire it with the moduleLoader DI pattern. The secret column stores only ciphertext. Criteria 3 (shape), 9, 39, 40. Unit tests for the repository with a mocked Prisma client. **Needs a yes before editing `schema.prisma`** (project rule). ~250 lines. Verifiable without the dev server.

### 2. Local Keycloak test provider and realm (S, Sprint 3)

Add a compose file and a realm export with one client (`cal-diy`, confidential, redirect URI `http://localhost:3000/api/auth/callback/*`) and three users: verified email, unverified email, no email claim. Add a README with exact start and stop commands and the values to paste into the admin page. Where the compose service lives is an owner's call (ADR-008). Criterion 42. ~150 lines, mostly JSON.

### 3. Admin provider service and tRPC procedures (M, Sprint 3)

Add `OidcProviderService`: field validation (criteria 3, 4), secret encryption with `symmetricEncrypt` and a clear error when `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is bad (6, 10), and `testDiscovery` with a 5-second timeout that returns one of the results in criterion 5. Add `viewer.admin.oidcProviders.{list,create,update,setEnabled,delete,testDiscovery}` on `authedAdminProcedure`; `list` returns a DTO with no secret field (2, 6). Enabling requires a passing discovery test. Unit tests cover each validation error, each discovery result and the non-admin `FORBIDDEN` path. ~400 lines with tests. Verifiable without the dev server.

### 4. Admin "Identity providers" settings page (M, Sprint 3)

Add `settings/(admin-layout)/admin/identity-providers/page.tsx` with the `ADMIN` role check in the page, and a view in `apps/web/modules/settings/admin/`. List providers; add and edit form with inline errors; write-only secret field ("Secret is set" / "Replace secret"); callback URL with copy button; Test connection button with its result; enable and disable switch; reorder. Every string in `common.json`. Criteria 1–9. Delete with typed confirmation moves to row 9. ~400 lines. Needs a browser.

### 5. Load providers per request and create new OIDC users (M, Sprint 3)

Make the NextAuth route handler async: load enabled providers through the repository and pass them to `getOptions` as `dynamicProviders` (ADR-001). Build each as a next-auth `oauth` provider with `wellKnown`, `idToken: true`, PKCE and state, a 5-second HTTP timeout, and no dangerous email linking. Map the `oidc-` prefix to `IdentityProvider.OIDC`. Add `OidcSignInService`, called from the top of `signIn` and `jwt` (ADR-005): reject unverified (15), missing email (16), name fallback (17), sign-up rules (18), create the user and `Account` row (14), find returning users by (provider, `sub`) (19), keep TOTP (20), and reject any email match with `oidc-account-exists` (27, Sprint 3 rule). Create the user and `Account` row in one transaction; leave `identityProviderId` null. A test per branch, including criterion 28 (no path reaches the shared lookups or auto-merge code) and a two-providers-one-`sub` test (criterion 30). Rules 1–4 from the Deep review in ADR-005 apply. ~450 lines with tests. **Gets a narrow Deep review of the `signIn` and `jwt` changes before merge.** Verifiable with unit tests; the demo needs row 2.

### 6. Login page buttons and sign-in error messages (S, Sprint 3)

Pass enabled providers (id and display name only) from the login and sign-up `getServerSideProps`. Render one "Continue with <name>" button per provider after Microsoft, with `useLastUsed` (11, 12). Read `error` from the URL on the login page and show messages for `OAuthSignin`, `OAuthCallback` and `AccessDenied` (21–25). Add the new error codes to `/auth/error` (`missing-email`, `oidc-signup-not-allowed`, `oidc-account-exists`, `unknown-provider`). ~200 lines. Needs a browser.

### 7. Link OIDC to existing accounts (M, Sprint 4)

Implement the customer's answer to Q1 and Q8 inside `OidcSignInService`: domain-based auto-link or reject, never for `ADMIN` accounts, invited-user rule, two providers with one email (30), email change at the provider (31). Calls `linkAccount` inside `signIn` so that next-auth finds the account by (provider, `sub`). **Gets a narrow Deep review.** Criteria 27–32. ~300 lines with tests.

### 8. Connected logins in Settings → Security (M, Sprint 4)

List linked providers with link dates (33). "Link" starts the flow for the signed-in user with `prompt=login` and adds an `Account` row to that user, with a clear error if the `sub` is linked elsewhere (34). Needs the `getSessionUserId` getter in `getOptions` (ADR-005, rule 3). "Unlink" is disabled when it is the last login method and explains the set-password flow (35). ~350 lines. Needs a browser.

### 9. Provider removal, password-login switch, end-to-end tests (M, Sprint 4)

Delete with typed confirmation and linked-user counts (36, 37), disable keeps links (38). If the customer wants it (Q4), the password-login switch with the admin break-glass rule (41). Playwright test against the Keycloak realm for criteria 14 and 15 (43). May split into two PRs if the switch is in scope. ~400 lines.

## Load notes for the team

- Zachary also owns #130 this sprint.
- Sprint 2 carryovers are in `docs/sprint3/carryovers.md`; owners of those may want a smaller row.
- Rows 1, 3, 5 suit someone who prefers backend and unit tests. Rows 4, 6 need someone who runs the dev server. Row 2 needs Docker.

# OIDC Sign-In Future Work

Ideas and enhancements deferred from the initial implementation.

## Enhancements

- Map provider groups or claims to Cal.diy roles and teams (customer Q9).
- Single logout at the provider (out of scope in #131).
- Per-provider button icon and color.
- API v2 endpoints for provider management.
- Show the last sign-in error and time for each provider on the admin page.

## Technical Debt

- If the per-request provider query shows in profiles, add a cache behind the repository with cross-instance invalidation (ADR-001, option 2).
- The secret uses AES-256-CBC without authentication, like other stored credentials. Moving all of them to an authenticated mode is a separate change.

## Nice to Have

- A mock OIDC server for CI, if Keycloak is too heavy for CI runs (ADR-008, option 3).

# OIDC Sign-In Implementation

## Status: spec draft (no product code)

## Completed

- Draft spec: `design.md` (43 acceptance criteria), `decisions.md` (ADR-001 to ADR-009), `customer-questions.md`, `breakdown.md`.
- Code reading on `origin/main` at `e01d161c0c` (facts in design.md, Technical Design).

## In Progress

- Team review of the breakdown and owners.
- Customer questions not yet posted on #131.

## Blocked

- Sub-issue 7 (account linking) waits on customer Q1 and Q8.
- Sub-issue 1 waits on a yes for the `schema.prisma` change.
- Sub-issue 9's password-login switch waits on customer Q4.

## Sprint 3 slice (demo by 2026-11-19)

Path: an admin adds one Keycloak provider in **Settings → Admin → Identity providers** (secret encrypted), the login page shows "Continue with <name>", a user with a verified email signs in against the local Keycloak and gets a new Cal.diy account, and a user with an unverified email sees the `unverified-email` message. A first login whose email matches an existing account is rejected with `oidc-account-exists`; that is the safe rule under every answer to Q1, so the slice does not wait on the customer.

Sub-issues on the path and merge order:

1. Sub-issue 1 (data model and repository). Everything else needs it.
2. Sub-issue 3 (admin service and tRPC) and sub-issue 5 (per-request providers and new-user sign-in), in parallel.
3. Sub-issue 4 (admin page, after 3) and sub-issue 6 (login buttons and errors, after 5).
4. Sub-issue 2 (Keycloak) at any time; the demo needs it.

Demo script: start Keycloak; sign in as the instance admin; add the provider; Test connection; enable; sign out; click the button; sign in as the verified Keycloak user (new account, onboarding); sign out; sign in as the unverified user (error page).

Moves to Sprint 4: sub-issues 7, 8, 9 (linking, settings page, removal with counts, password-login switch, Playwright test).

Risk: sub-issue 5 is the largest and touches the 1,255-line `next-auth-options.ts`. Start it on day one after sub-issue 1 merges. Keep the change to that file to two delegation calls (top of `signIn`, top of `jwt`) and the `getOptions` argument.

## Deep review
```

# Zach's proposed split of #131 (PR #133 and sub-issue #136)

**Where things stand:** PR #133 is a draft and documentation only (555 lines under `specs/oidc-sign-in/`). It has the full spec (`design.md`, 43 acceptance criteria), 9 decision records, the customer questions, a breakdown into sub-issues, and a Sprint 3 plan. Issue #136 is the first sub-issue, assigned to Zach. No other sub-issues exist yet, the Owner column is empty, and the breakdown hasn't been posted on #131. The instructor asked for that comment, and there are 7 days left before the demo.

Timing matters here. Zach wrote the spec on Nov 11, and the customer answered the questions **today (Nov 12)**. Parts of the spec are now out of date (see the gaps section).

## His breakdown

| # | Sub-issue | Size | Depends on | Sprint |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | OIDC provider data model and repository (**#136**) | M | none | 3 |
| 2 | Local Keycloak test provider, realm and README | S | none | 3 |
| 3 | Admin provider service and tRPC (validation, secret encryption, "Test connection" discovery check, 10-provider limit) | M | 1 | 3 |
| 4 | Admin "Identity providers" settings page (list, add/edit, write-only secret, copy callback URL, test, enable, reorder) | M | 3 | 3 |
| 5 | Load providers per request and create new OIDC users (`OidcSignInService`) | M | 1 | 3 |
| 6 | Login page buttons and sign-in error messages | S | 5 | 3 |
| 7 | Link OIDC to existing accounts (customer's linking and invite rules) | M | 5 | 4 |
| 8 | Connected logins in Settings → Security (link and unlink) | M | 7 | 4 |
| 9 | Provider removal, password-login switch, Playwright end-to-end tests | M | 4, 7 | 4 |

**Merge order:** 1 → (3 ∥ 5) → (4 after 3, 6 after 5). Row 2 can merge any time.

**Sprint 3 demo:**
1. An admin adds a Keycloak provider in the UI.
2. "Continue with \<name\>" appears on the login page.
3. A user with a verified email signs in and gets a new account.
4. A user with an unverified email sees an error.
5. A login whose email matches an existing account is rejected for now (`oidc-account-exists`). That's safe whatever the linking rule turns out to be.

**How it compares to my overview:** it lines up almost one-to-one. Rows 1/3/4/6 match my Phases 1/2/6/5, row 7 is my Phase 4 linking, and row 8 is Phase 7. The main differences:
- His row 5 combines my Phases 3 and 4 (per-request providers plus the sign-in policy).
- He found a real problem my overview only touched on. If an OIDC user's `sub` were stored in `User.identityProviderId`, it could collide across providers through the shared lookups in `signIn` and `jwt`. ADR-005 and criterion 28 handle this by leaving `identityProviderId` null and routing OIDC around every existing lookup and auto-merge path.
- His design uses provider IDs (`oidc-<cuid>`) in the callback URL, so the URL is immutable. That resolves the slug concern I raised.

## #136 (sub-issue 1) in brief

- **Schema:** adds `OIDC` to the `IdentityProvider` enum and creates an `OidcProvider` table with `displayName`, `issuer`, `clientId`, `clientSecretEncrypted`, `scopes`, `allowSignup`, `allowedDomains[]`, `enabled`, `position`, and an audit field `updatedById`.
- **Unique pair:** `issuer` + `clientId` must be unique.
- **Repository:** `PrismaOidcProviderRepository`, wired through DI. Only `findByIdWithEncryptedSecret` ever selects the secret.
- **Delete:** `deleteWithAccounts` removes the provider and its `Account` links in one transaction.
- **Size:** about 300 lines across 6–8 files. Encryption and validation are left to sub-issue 3.

It's well specified and follows the repo rules (`select` only, DTOs, DI, ≥2 alternatives per decision).

## Gaps from today's customer answers

These are where #133 and #136 now conflict with or miss what the customer said:

1. **#136's schema is missing two fields the customer now requires:**
   - **Owned domains (for auto-linking, answer 1).** This is a different setting from `allowedDomains`, which controls sign-up. "Who may create an account" and "whose existing account we may auto-link" are separate settings.
   - **"Accept this provider's MFA" (answer 6).**

   Adding them now costs a few lines. Adding them later means a second migration and another schema approval. I'd raise this on #136 before it's implemented.
2. **2FA conflicts with today's code.** The spec proposed exempting OIDC users from 2FA, because `requiresTwoFactorSetup` exempts every non-`CAL` user. The customer instead wants cal.diy 2FA *required* unless the provider's MFA is accepted and `amr` shows a second factor. No row covers this. Also, unless row 5 handles it, Sprint 3 OIDC users would skip a site-wide "require 2FA" setting. Worth deciding whether that's acceptable for the demo.
3. **Global "disable signup" isn't covered.** Criterion 18 only checks the provider switch and the domain list. The customer said the global setting wins, so row 5 needs to check the same flags as `apps/web/app/api/auth/signup/route.ts:29-31`.
4. **Invites are handled the opposite way.** Criterion 29 treats an invited email as an existing account (reject). The customer says a verified OIDC login **accepts the invite**, even when sign-up is off. That's row 7, so the Sprint 3 behavior is fine, but the criterion needs rewriting.
5. **Forgot password for OIDC users.** Criterion 37 says "to confirm in implementation". The customer explicitly asked for a test, so it should be an acceptance criterion in row 9.
6. **Row 9 is now too big.** The password-login switch is confirmed (answer 4), and the MFA and forgot-password items need a home. Row 9 should split, for example: 9a removal + forgot-password test, 9b password-login switch + provider MFA, 9c Playwright end-to-end tests.
7. **The customer questions are now answered.** `customer-questions.md` and ADR-004 ("left to the customer") should be updated with the answers.

## Next steps for the team

- Fill in owners.
- Fold the answers into the spec (items 1–7 above).
- Post the breakdown comment on #131.
- Create sub-issues 2–6 today. Rows 3 and 5 can't start until #136 merges, and row 5 (around 450 lines, touching the 1,255-line `next-auth-options.ts`) is the demo's critical path.

One practical note for #136's criterion 13: `yarn type-check:ci` doesn't work on your Windows machine, so whoever verifies it there will need the turbo-based alternative.

```text
import type { PageProps } from "app/_types";
import { _generateMetadata, getTranslate } from "app/_utils";
import Link from "next/link";
import { z } from "zod";

import { IdentityProvider } from "@calcom/prisma/enums";
import { Button } from "@calcom/ui/components/button";
import { XIcon } from "@coss/ui/icons";

import AuthContainer from "@components/ui/AuthContainer";

export const generateMetadata = async () => {
  return await _generateMetadata(
    (t) => t("error"),
    () => "",
    undefined,
    undefined,
    "/auth/error"
  );
};

const querySchema = z.object({
  error: z.string().optional(),
  provider: z.string().optional(),
});

const ServerPage = async ({ searchParams }: PageProps) => {
  const t = await getTranslate();

  const { error, provider } = querySchema.parse({
    error: (await searchParams)?.error || undefined,
    provider: (await searchParams)?.provider || undefined,
  });

  // generate error message based on different errors
  const getErrorMessage = (error: string | undefined, provider: string | undefined) => {
    if (error === "user-creation-error") {
      return t("user_creation_error");
    } else if (error === "wrong-provider") {
      // showing user their original identity provider by which account is managed.
      const providerName =
        provider === IdentityProvider.GOOGLE
          ? "Google"
          : provider === IdentityProvider.CAL
            ? "Email and Password"
            : provider === IdentityProvider.SAML
              ? "SAML (like Okta)"
              : "your original login method";
      return t("account_managed_by_identity_provider_error", { provider: providerName });
    } else if (error === "saml-idp-not-authoritative") {
      return t("saml_idp_not_authoritative_error");
    } else if (error === "unverified-email") {
      return t("unverified_email_oauth_error");
    }
    return t("error_during_login") + (error ? ` Error code: ${error}` : "");
  };

  const errorMsg = getErrorMessage(error, provider);

  return (
    <AuthContainer>
      <div>
        <div className="bg-error mx-auto flex h-12 w-12 items-center justify-center rounded-full">
          <XIcon className="h-6 w-6 text-red-600" />
        </div>
        <div className="mt-3 text-center sm:mt-5">
          <h3 className="text-emphasis text-lg font-medium leading-6" id="modal-title">
            {errorMsg}
          </h3>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div className="mt-5 sm:mt-6">
        <Link href="/auth/login">
          <Button className="flex w-full justify-center">{t("go_back_login")}</Button>
        </Link>
      </div>
    </AuthContainer>
  );
};
```

# Recommendation for tonight: sub-issue 6 (login page buttons and sign-in error messages)

I agree a UI sub-issue is the right call, and row 6 is the one that fits both goals.

## Why row 6

- **Most of it has no dependencies, so it can be finished and tested tonight.**
  - The error-message half doesn't need any OIDC code. `login-view.tsx` only reads `callbackUrl` and `email` from the URL (`:140`, `:255`), never `?error=`. So when NextAuth sends someone back with `OAuthSignin`, `OAuthCallback` or `AccessDenied`, they see nothing. That gap already affects Google login today. You can test the fix in a browser by visiting `/auth/login?error=OAuthCallback`.
  - The new `/auth/error` codes (`missing-email`, `oidc-signup-not-allowed`, `oidc-account-exists`, `unknown-provider`) are just more branches in `getErrorMessage` in `apps/web/app/(use-page-wrapper)/auth/error/page.tsx`.
- **The button half needs one small piece of wiring.** Have the login view take an `oidcProviders: { id, displayName }[]` prop and render "Continue with \<name\>" after the Microsoft button (`login-view.tsx:224`), calling `signIn(\`oidc-${id}\`)`. With an empty list nothing renders, so the PR is safe on its own. The only dependency is one call to `findEnabled()` in `apps/web/server/lib/auth/login/getServerSideProps.tsx`, which needs #136's repository. Add that as a final commit once #136 merges. The PR can't merge before #136 anyway.
- **It's on the demo path.** The demo's last two steps (click the button, see the unverified-email error) are this sub-issue. It's also small (about 200 lines in about 5 files), so it won't take long to review this week.
- **It gives you something to mutation-test.** Pull the error-code → message mapping out into a pure function with unit tests. That's a good StrykerJS candidate, which Sprint 3 asks each member to have on one issue.

## Why not the others tonight

- **Row 4 (admin page):** it's the other UI option and more visible in the demo. But it depends on row 3, which depends on #136, and neither has a PR yet. You'd be building a roughly 400-line page against tRPC procedures that don't exist. It's a better candidate for later this week, once row 3 has a PR.
- **Row 2 (Keycloak):** it has no dependencies and is just as doable tonight. Everyone needs it to test, so it's a strong pick for a teammate. It's not UI, though.

## Two things to watch

1. **Overlap with #136.** Its criterion 13 also edits `auth/error/page.tsx` (adding an OIDC case to the provider-name check). Ask Zach to drop that from #136 and let row 6 own the file, to avoid a merge conflict.
2. **Medium-issue minimum.** Row 6 is sized S. If you need two medium sub-issues for your personal minimum, plan to also take a medium later (row 4, or row 8 in Sprint 4).

```text
### Step 1 — Gather

  - the course's verbatim "Feature issue — user story" or "Bug report" template from the sprint reference file.

### Step 2 — Draft `.claude/work/issue-<N>/spec.md`
**Repo template first, then the course sections:**
1. **The repo template's sections, filled in briefly.**
   - Feature: "Is your proposal related to a problem?", "Describe the solution you'd like", "Describe alternatives you've considered", "Additional context", "Requirement/Document".
   - Bug: "Issue Summary", "Steps to Reproduce", "Actual Results", "Expected Results", "Technical details", "Evidence".
   - Keep them short and point to the course sections below rather than repeating them.
2. **The course template's sections, word for word for every heading and the user-story sentence frame.**
   - Feature: `## User Story` (As a … I want … so that …), `## User Scenario`, `## Acceptance Criteria` (numbered, at least 3), `## Out of Scope`, `## Open Questions`.
   - Bug: `## Observed Behavior (OB)`, `## Expected Behavior (EB)`, `## Steps to Reproduce (S2R)`, `## Additional Information`.

Headings must match the template exactly. For example, use `## Open Questions` (plural), as `/pr-preflight` checks.

**How to build it, so the wording can't drift:**
1. Make the course part with the fill script:
   - `node .claude/course/scripts/template-fill.mjs --slots feature-issue` (or `bug-report`) to see the numbered blanks and template lines;
   - write the values to `.claude/work/issue-<N>/spec-values.json`. Use `"lines"` to replace the template's `1. ...` placeholder lines with the real numbered criteria and bullets;
   - `node .claude/course/scripts/template-fill.mjs feature-issue .claude/work/issue-<N>/spec-values.json .claude/work/issue-<N>/spec-course.md`.
2. Write `spec.md` as the repo-template sections, followed by the **unchanged** contents of `spec-course.md`.
3. Run `node .claude/course/scripts/template-verify.mjs feature-issue .claude/work/issue-<N>/spec.md`. It must say OK. Run it again after any edit, including edits the user asks for.

One allowed grammar fix: if the user type starts with a vowel sound, change "As a" to "As an" ("As an event host"). The checker accepts it.

### Step 3 — Self-check (show it in chat)
- **INVEST,** one line each: Independent, Negotiable, Valuable, Estimable, Small, Testable. Say which ones are weak and why.

- **Ambiguities** go under `## Open Questions`, not guessed answers.

# Course skill rules (loaded by every course skill)

These rules override anything else in a skill. If a step seems to need breaking one, stop and ask.

1. **No git or GitHub writes, ever. The user does these by hand.** Never commit, add, push, pull, create/switch/delete branches, checkout, stash, merge, rebase, reset, tag, open/edit/close/review/merge PRs, post or edit issue/PR comments, or change labels, milestones or releases. Deny rules in `.claude/settings.local.json` block these too; never try to get around them (no `git -C`, `bash -c`, scripts, or `gh api` writes). Instead give:
   - draft markdown (PR descriptions, issue bodies, comments, review rubrics, release notes) saved under `.claude/work/`;
   - a draft commit message;
   - the exact commands for the user to run, each with a one-line note on what it does.
2. **Read-only git and `gh` are fine:** `git status/diff/log/show/fetch/rev-parse/ls-files/cat-file/ls-remote`, `gh issue view/list`, `gh pr view/list/diff/checks`, plain `gh api <path>` (GET). Read the current branch with `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` (`git branch` is denied).
3. **Local files are fine:** drafts and notes under `.claude/work/` (per-issue notes in `.claude/work/issue-<N>/`), log copies under `ai-logs/…`, diagrams and check-ins under `docs/…`. Never delete or overwrite an existing file without asking.

   `--list` shows the template names. A draft that fails verification is not done.

6. **Code review scores (1–10) stay blank** for the human reviewer. Draft observations in the Notes column only. Never draft a review of a PR the user authored, and never approve or merge.
7. **Story points are suggestions** for team planning poker, not final values.
```

## AI logging procedure

Log every project-related AI session as a full transcript, named `YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<short-slug>.md`, in `ai-logs/sprint3/<your-github-username>/` — never in a teammate's folder. Link each log from the issue or PR it documents.

**What to log.** Writing, debugging or reviewing code; understanding the codebase or an issue; drafting issues, PR descriptions or docs; design discussions; configuring tools (including the mutation tool). Unproductive sessions count too. Not required: purely academic questions, unrelated research, or clarifying assignment instructions. When in doubt, log it.

**File name parts.** Date = the day the session started (`2026-11-05`). Tool = identifier below. Slug = brief, lowercase, hyphens (`issue-42-auth-fix`).

| Tool | Identifier | How to capture |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Code (CLI) | `claude-code` | `specstory run claude` |
| Gemini CLI | `gemini-cli` | `specstory run gemini` |
| OpenAI Codex CLI | `codex-cli` | `specstory run codex` |
| Cursor (IDE or CLI) | `cursor` | `specstory run cursor` (CLI) or SpecStory VS Code extension |
| GitHub Copilot (VS Code) | `copilot` | SpecStory VS Code extension |
| Claude.ai (web) | `claude-web` | Claude Exporter Chrome extension, export as Markdown |
| ChatGPT (web) | `chatgpt` | ChatGPT Exporter extension |
| Claude Desktop app | `claude-desktop` | Copy manually into .md; note in the log it was captured manually |
| Other | `other-<name>` | Gemini Exporter / Grok Exporter, or manual transcript |

**SpecStory setup.** macOS/Linux: `brew tap specstoryai/tap` then `brew install specstory`. Windows: download `SpecStoryCLI_Windows_x86_64.zip` from the releases page, extract, add to `PATH`, verify with `specstory version`. Forgot to wrap a session? Run `specstory sync`.

**Every log must contain:**

- The model/tool used (e.g. "Claude Sonnet 4.5 via Claude Code")
- Full prompt and response history, with timestamps
- For agentic tools: all file edits and commands run (SpecStory captures these)
- For web chat: any files or text pasted as context, inline or in the attachments folder
- Manual transcripts: every message labeled `[User]` or `[AI]` with timestamps

**Not accepted:** session summaries; paraphrased prompts; share links to a chat (they may accompany a log, not replace it); tool output without the prompts that produced it; `.html`, `.docx` or `.pdf` logs; screenshots; reconstructions after the fact. Accepted formats are `.md` (preferred), `.txt` and `.json`.

**Attachments.** Put files, screenshots or PDFs used as context in a folder with the log's name minus `.md`:

```
ai-logs/sprint3/jsmith/2026-11-05_claude-web_understanding-issue-42.md
ai-logs/sprint3/jsmith/2026-11-05_claude-web_understanding-issue-42/
    architecture-screenshot.png
    relevant-code-snippet.txt
```

```text
## ADR-001: How providers reach NextAuth without a restart

Status: Proposed.

### Context

Today `providers` is a module-level array built once at import (`next-auth-options.ts:307–370`), and `getOptions` is synchronous. Criterion 1 requires a change to take effect on the next login with no restart. `apps/web/pages/api/auth/[...nextauth].ts` already calls `NextAuth(req, res, getOptions(...))` on every request, so options can differ per request.

### Options Considered

1. **Load enabled providers from the database on each `/api/auth/*` request.** The handler awaits a repository call, then passes the result to `getOptions`. Pros: always current, no invalidation logic, correct on several server instances. Cons: one indexed query per auth request (sign-in, callback, session, CSRF). Auth traffic is small next to booking traffic, and the table holds at most 10 rows.
2. **Cache providers in memory with invalidation on admin save.** Pros: no query on most requests. Cons: each server instance has its own cache, so a save on instance A is stale on instance B until a TTL expires; this breaks criterion 1 on any multi-instance deploy unless we add Redis pub/sub. More code to review.
3. **Build providers at boot from the database.** Pros: no change to `getOptions`. Cons: needs a restart, which fails criterion 1.

### Decision

Option 1. `getOptions` gains a `dynamicProviders: Provider[]` argument and stays synchronous, so its other callers do not change. Only the NextAuth route handler awaits the load. If a profile shows the query matters, add option 2 behind the same repository method later (recorded in `future-work.md`).

### Consequences

- Every caller of `getOptions` must be checked. Callers that do not handle sign-in (for example session decoding) pass an empty list.
- A database outage also breaks OIDC sign-in. Password login already needs the database, so this adds no new failure mode.
```

# Sub-issue 6: login buttons and sign-in errors, and whether `/plan-spec` is current

## 1. What sub-issue 6 does

Sub-issue 6 is the part of #131 that users see when they log in. Everything else in #131 is either admin setup (rows 1–4) or server logic (rows 5 and 7). Row 6 does two things.

**A. Shows a sign-in button for each provider.** The login page shows one "Continue with \<display name\>" button for each enabled OIDC provider, in the order the admin set, below Google and Microsoft. Clicking it hands off to NextAuth (`signIn("oidc-<id>")`), which redirects to the identity provider. When no provider is enabled, the page looks exactly as it does today (criterion 11, which covers the "nothing changes after upgrade" answer, #13). The sign-up page shows the same buttons, but only for providers with "allow new accounts" on (criterion 12).

**B. Explains failures.** When a sign-in fails, the user gets a clear message instead of a blank page. There are two places failures land:
- **The login page (`/auth/login?error=…`).** NextAuth sends its built-in errors here: `OAuthSignin` (couldn't start the flow, for example because the provider is down), `OAuthCallback` (the token exchange failed, for example because of a wrong secret or a bad `state`), and `AccessDenied`. **Confirmed:** `login-view.tsx` never reads `error` from the URL. It only reads `callbackUrl` and `email` (`:140`, `:255`). So these failures show nothing today, for Google and Microsoft too. That's an existing bug, and row 6 fixes it.
- **The error page (`/auth/error?error=…`).** cal.diy's own `signIn` callback sends its errors here. Row 6 adds messages for the new codes that row 5 will emit: `missing-email`, `oidc-signup-not-allowed`, `oidc-account-exists`, `unknown-provider`. `unverified-email` already has one (`auth/error/page.tsx`, the `getErrorMessage` branches).

One way to put it: rows 1–5 make OIDC sign-in work, and row 6 makes it usable. In the demo, row 6 covers the click on the button at the start and the error message at the end.

## 2. How it relates to the other sub-issues

```
 #136 (row 1) repository ──findEnabled()──▶ row 6 (buttons) ◀── row 4 sets displayName / order / enabled
                                              │  ▲
                        signIn("oidc-<id>")   │  │  error codes in the URL
                                              ▼  │
                         row 5 (NextAuth registers oidc-<id>, OidcSignInService decides)
```

Row 6 depends on contracts with three other rows. The spec should state each one explicitly:

| Contract | With | What row 6 relies on |
|---|---|---|
| Provider data | #136 | `findEnabled()` returns `OidcProviderPublicDto` (`id`, `displayName`, `allowSignup`, …) in admin order, **with no secret**. Row 6 sends only `id` and `displayName` to the browser. |
| Provider ID format | Row 5 | The NextAuth provider is registered as `oidc-<id>`. If row 5 picks another format, the buttons break. |
| Error codes | Row 5 | Row 5 *emits* the codes and row 6 *displays* them. Criteria 23–25 (wrong secret, provider disabled mid-flow, unknown ID) are mostly row 5's behavior; row 6 only owns the message text. |
| Display name and order | Row 4 | Comes indirectly through the table. Row 6 doesn't depend on row 4's code. |

**Practical result:** row 6 can be fully built and tested tonight with a hard-coded provider list in a unit test. The live wiring (`findEnabled()` in server props) is one small commit after #136 merges. The buttons only work end to end once row 5 has merged.

## 3. Systems touched and how they change

All of these are **Confirmed** by reading the code.

| File | Today | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `apps/web/server/lib/auth/login/getServerSideProps.tsx:88-93` | Returns `isGoogleLoginEnabled`, `isOutlookLoginEnabled` (hard-coded `false`), `csrfToken`, `totpEmail` | Add `oidcProviders: { id, displayName }[]` from `getOidcProviderRepository().findEnabled()`. Wrap it in try/catch so a database problem returns `[]` and never breaks the login page (matches criterion 26). |
| `apps/web/modules/auth/login-view.tsx` | `:173` `showSocialLogin = isGoogleLoginEnabled \|\| isOutlookLoginEnabled`; Google button `:198-214`, Microsoft `:215-230`, then an "or" divider | (1) Include OIDC in `showSocialLogin`, or an OIDC-only instance shows no buttons and no divider. (2) Render the OIDC buttons after Microsoft, following the same pattern: `setLastUsed`, `signIn(\`oidc-${id}\`, { callbackUrl })`, `<LastUsed />`. (3) Read `searchParams.get("error")` and show a message for `OAuthSignin`, `OAuthCallback`, `AccessDenied`, falling back to a generic one. |
| `apps/web/modules/auth/hooks/useLastUsed.tsx:7` | `type LoginType = "saml" \| "google" \| "microsoft" \| "credentials"` | Widen it to accept `` `oidc-${string}` `` so the "last used" badge works per provider. |
| `apps/web/lib/signup/getServerSideProps.tsx:58` | `isGoogleLoginEnabled` | Same `oidcProviders` prop, filtered to `allowSignup`. Also hide the buttons when global signup is disabled (customer answer 2). |
| `apps/web/modules/signup-view.tsx:632-734` | Google, Microsoft and divider blocks | Same buttons, same `showSocialLogin` fix. |
| `apps/web/app/(use-page-wrapper)/auth/error/page.tsx:39-56` | `getErrorMessage` if/else chain; the provider name falls back to "your original login method" | Add the four new codes. Add an `OIDC` case to the provider name (this overlaps #136's criterion 13; coordinate with Zach). |
| `packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json` | n/a | Add `continue_with_provider` (with a `{{provider}}` slot) and one key per message. |
| New helper and test, e.g. `apps/web/modules/auth/lib/signInErrorMessage.ts` plus `.test.ts` | n/a | A pure function mapping error code to translation key, unit-tested. It's also a good mutation-testing target. |

That's about **7–9 files and roughly 200–300 lines** including tests, which is between small and medium. If you need it to count as medium, the honest justification is that it changes four surfaces (login, sign-up, error page, server props for both pages). The course warns that overstated scope can be reclassified, though.

**Things the spec has to settle:**
1. **Criterion 22 wants the provider's name in the message** ("We could not reach \<display name\>…"). NextAuth's `?error=OAuthSignin` redirect doesn't say which provider failed. The options are: a generic message (simplest), using the `lastUsed` value from local storage (set just before the click, though it can be wrong), or asking row 5 to add a custom redirect parameter. This is a real design decision with alternatives.
2. **Whether the sign-up page (criterion 12) belongs in tonight's PR.** Dropping it keeps the PR small. Keeping it makes the sign-up flow consistent for the demo.
3. **What `OAuthCallback` should say.** It covers several different failures (bad `state`, wrong secret, replay), and row 6 can't tell them apart without row 5's help.

```text
### Is your proposal related to a problem?
```

```markdown
Sub-issue 6 of #131. Seed and criteria numbers come from `specs/oidc-sign-in/` in PR #133 (criteria 11, 12, 21–25 in `design.md`).

#131 lets an admin add OIDC providers, but users have no way to reach them: the login and sign-up pages only render the hard-coded Google and Microsoft buttons (`apps/web/modules/auth/login-view.tsx:198-230`, `apps/web/modules/signup-view.tsx:632-734`).

Sign-in failures are also invisible today. When NextAuth cannot start or finish an OAuth flow, it redirects to `/auth/login?error=OAuthSignin` (or `OAuthCallback`, `AccessDenied`), but `login-view.tsx` never reads `error` from the URL (it only reads `callbackUrl` and `email`, `:140` and `:255`), so the user sees a normal login page with no explanation. This already affects Google and Microsoft sign-in, and it would affect every OIDC failure (provider down, wrong client secret, expired `state`). The `/auth/error` page also has no messages for the new OIDC error codes that sub-issue 5 will emit.

### Describe the solution you'd like

1. **Provider buttons.** The login page shows one "Continue with <display name>" button per enabled OIDC provider, in the admin's order, below Google and Microsoft. Clicking it calls `signIn("oidc-<id>")`. The sign-up page shows the same buttons only for providers with "allow new accounts" on, and none when sign-up is disabled site-wide. With no enabled provider, both pages look exactly as they do today. Only each provider's `id` and display name reach the browser.
2. **Login page errors.** The login page reads `?error=` and shows a clear, translated message for `OAuthSignin`, `OAuthCallback` and `AccessDenied`, with a generic fallback for anything else.
3. **Error page messages.** `/auth/error` shows messages for the new codes `missing-email`, `oidc-signup-not-allowed`, `oidc-account-exists` and `unknown-provider`, and names OIDC accounts correctly in the existing `wrong-provider` message.

All new strings go in `packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json`. The full spec (user story, scenario, acceptance criteria, out of scope, open questions) will be added to this issue before coding, and a teammate will post a spec review.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

- **Show errors only on `/auth/error`.** We could point NextAuth's `pages.error` at `/auth/error` for every failure instead of reading `?error=` on the login page. We prefer the login page, because the user can retry or pick another sign-in method right there. The choice will be recorded in the design decisions.
- **Name the provider in failure messages ("We could not reach <name>").** NextAuth's `?error=` redirect does not say which provider failed. The options (a generic message, the "last used" value, or a parameter added by sub-issue 5) will be decided in the spec.

### Additional context

- Parent: #131. Depends on #136 (sub-issue 1) for `findEnabled()`. The buttons work end to end only after sub-issue 5 registers providers as `oidc-<id>` and emits the error codes above.
- The PR can open before #136 merges: the button list comes in as a prop (empty means no buttons), and the error handling has no dependency. Wiring the props to `findEnabled()` is a final commit after #136 merges.
- Coordination: #136's criterion 13 also edits `apps/web/app/(use-page-wrapper)/auth/error/page.tsx`. Proposed: this sub-issue owns that change.
- Out of scope: the NextAuth provider registration and sign-in rules (sub-issue 5), the admin page (sub-issue 4), and linking or unlinking from settings (sub-issue 8).

### Requirement/Document

- Feature spec: `specs/oidc-sign-in/design.md` (PR #133), criteria 11, 12, 21–25.
- NextAuth error codes: https://next-auth.js.org/configuration/pages#sign-in-page

## Scope

Small. It touches the login and sign-up views and their server props, the `/auth/error` page, the `useLastUsed` login type, and translations: about 7–9 files and 200–300 lines including unit tests. It changes no schema, API or sign-in logic.
```

```markdown
# Issue #146 — handoff context for implementation planning

#146 = sub-issue 6 of #131 (OIDC sign-in): login/sign-up provider buttons + sign-in error messages. Owner: dchan01-wm.
Written 2026-11-18 from an earlier session's research (Nov 12) plus a fresh GitHub check. Code facts were traced at commit `e01d161c0c`-era `main`; re-check line numbers before editing.

## Where everything lives

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| #146 issue text (repo template + Scope) — same text as the GitHub body | `.claude/work/issue-131-sub6/issue.md` |
| Parent feature, customer answers (13 Q&A, Nov 12) | GitHub #131 comments (`gh issue view 131 --comments`) |
| Full feature spec by Zach: 43 acceptance criteria, ADR-001..009, breakdown, Sprint 3 slice | PR #133, branch `docs/oidc-spec`, folder `specs/oidc-sign-in/` (`design.md`, `decisions.md`, `breakdown.md`, `implementation.md`, `customer-questions.md`, `future-work.md`). Not on `main`; read with `gh pr diff 133` or `git show origin/docs/oidc-spec:specs/oidc-sign-in/design.md` |
| Sub-issue 1 spec (data model + repository, `findEnabled()` DTO) | GitHub #136 |
| Course rules / sprint config | `.claude/course/skill-rules.md`, `.claude/course/current-sprint.md`, `.claude/course/sprint3-reference.md` |

The earlier session's overview of OIDC, the client's asks, and the phase estimates were given in chat only; the essentials are summarized below.

## How #131 is decomposed (Zach's breakdown, PR #133 `breakdown.md`)

| # | Sub-issue | Size | Depends on | Sprint | GitHub |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | OIDC provider table + `PrismaOidcProviderRepository` | M | — | 3 | #136 (zach-short), open, **no PR yet** |
| 2 | Local Keycloak test provider + realm + README | S | — | 3 | #151, open, **unassigned** |
| 3 | Admin provider service + tRPC (validation, secret encryption, discovery test, 10-provider cap) | M | 1 | 3 | not created |
| 4 | Admin "Identity providers" settings page | M | 3 | 3 | not created |
| 5 | Load providers per request in NextAuth (`oidc-<id>`) + `OidcSignInService` (new users, verified-email rule) | M | 1 | 3 | not created |
| 6 | **Login/sign-up buttons + sign-in error messages** | S | 1 (data), 5 (end to end) | 3 | **#146** |
| 7 | Link OIDC to existing accounts (customer rules) | M | 5 | 4 | not created |
| 8 | Connected logins in Settings → Security | M | 7 | 4 | not created |
| 9 | Removal, password-login switch, Playwright e2e | M | 4, 7 | 4 | not created |

Merge order: 1 → (3 ∥ 5) → (4 after 3, 6 after 5); 2 any time.

## What #146 must deliver (from the issue body)

1. **Buttons.** Login page: one "Continue with <display name>" per enabled provider, admin order, below Google/Microsoft, `signIn("oidc-<id>", { callbackUrl })`. Sign-up page: same, only providers with `allowSignup`, none when sign-up is disabled site-wide. No providers → pages unchanged. Only `id` + `displayName` reach the browser.
2. **Login-page errors.** Read `?error=`; translated messages for `OAuthSignin`, `OAuthCallback`, `AccessDenied`; generic fallback.
3. **`/auth/error` messages** for `missing-email`, `oidc-signup-not-allowed`, `oidc-account-exists`, `unknown-provider`; OIDC name in `wrong-provider`.
All strings in `packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json`.
Feature-spec criteria it maps to: 11, 12, 21–25 in `specs/oidc-sign-in/design.md`.

## Code facts (Confirmed by reading, Nov 12)

- `apps/web/server/lib/auth/login/getServerSideProps.tsx:88-93` — props `csrfToken`, `isGoogleLoginEnabled`, `isOutlookLoginEnabled: false`, `totpEmail`. Add `oidcProviders`.
- `apps/web/modules/auth/login-view.tsx`
  - `:140`, `:255` — only `callbackUrl` / `email` read from the URL; `error` never read (existing bug, affects Google/Microsoft too).
  - `:131-137` — `errorMessages` map keyed by `ErrorCode`; `:161-170` credential-error handling.
  - `:173` — `showSocialLogin = isGoogleLoginEnabled || isOutlookLoginEnabled` → must include OIDC or an OIDC-only instance shows no buttons/divider.
  - `:198-214` Google button, `:215-230` Microsoft button (pattern: `setLastUsed`, `signIn`, `<LastUsed />`), then "or" divider.
- `apps/web/modules/auth/hooks/useLastUsed.tsx:7` — `type LoginType = "saml" | "google" | "microsoft" | "credentials"`; widen for `oidc-<id>`.
- `apps/web/lib/signup/getServerSideProps.tsx:58` — `isGoogleLoginEnabled`; add filtered `oidcProviders`.
- `apps/web/modules/signup-view.tsx:197-198` props, `:632`, `:683`, `:734` Google/Microsoft/divider blocks.
- `apps/web/app/(use-page-wrapper)/auth/error/page.tsx:39-56` — `getErrorMessage` if/else chain; provider-name fallback "your original login method".
- Sign-up disabled = `NEXT_PUBLIC_DISABLE_SIGNUP === "true"` OR feature flag `disable-signup` (`apps/web/app/api/auth/signup/route.ts:29-31`). `login-view.tsx:175` checks only the env var.
- NextAuth 4.24.13; error page config `pages.error: "/auth/error"` in `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` (`pages` block ~L410). Providers are a static module-level array today (`:307-370`); per-request loading is sub-issue 5 (ADR-001).

| Data | #136 | `getOidcProviderRepository().findEnabled()` → `OidcProviderPublicDto` (`id`, `displayName`, `allowSignup`, …), ordered by `position`, no secret. DTO in `packages/lib/dto/`. |

## Open decisions (need ≥2 alternatives each in design, user chooses)

1. Where NextAuth OAuth errors show: login page reading `?error=` (issue's preference) vs `/auth/error` for everything.
2. Naming the failed provider in messages: generic text vs `lastUsed` value vs a parameter added by sub-issue 5.
3. How to build/merge before #136 exists: prop-driven buttons with the `findEnabled()` wiring as a last commit vs stacking on #136's branch vs a temporary local type.
4. Whether the sign-up page (criterion 12) is in this PR or split out.
5. Whether to extract a pure `code → translation key` helper (unit-testable; mutation-testing candidate for D6).
```
